public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 701

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/701](https://www.erdosproblems.com/701)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos701

open Cardinal

/--
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a family of sets closed under taking subsets (i.e. if
$B\subseteq A\in\mathcal{F}$ then $B\in \mathcal{F}$). There exists some element $x$ such that
whenever $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq \mathcal{F}$ is an intersecting subfamily we have
$$\lvert \mathcal{F}'\rvert \leq \lvert \{ A\in \mathcal{F} : x\in A\}\rvert.$$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_701 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {X : Type} [Nonempty X] [Fintype X],
    ∀ (F : Set (Set X)), IsLowerSet F →
      ∃ x : X, ∀ᵉ (F' ⊆ F),
        F'.Intersecting →
          (#F' ≤ #{ A : Set X | A ∈ F ∧ x ∈ A }) := by
  sorry

end Erdos701

reformulations.difference: Chvátal's companion webpage counts {∅} as intersecting and excludes that hereditary base family. Lean instead uses Mathlib's all-pairs intersection convention, which excludes {∅} as an intersecting subfamily, and allows F = {∅}. The original 1974 paper's displayed intersection definition already agrees with Lean.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The intersection conventions differ only for the subfamily {∅}. When F = {∅}, Lean's only intersecting subfamily is empty, so its conclusion holds. For F ≠ {∅}, if {∅} ⊆ F, some nonempty A belongs to F. A star dominating all Mathlib-intersecting subfamilies must dominate {A}, hence has size at least one and also dominates {∅}. Thus excluding the exceptional base family under the distinct-pairs convention gives an equivalent full conjecture. This equivalence was proved without sorry as Review701.full_convention_equiv in /workspace/review/equivalence.lean.

review.notes: The sole theorem faithfully states the problem. Chvátal's original conjecture explicitly uses a finite ground set, supporting [Fintype X]; [Nonempty X] prevents an impossible element choice on an empty ground type. Checked downward closure, intersection semantics, cardinalities, quantifier scope, and answer polarity. Lean verified the empty-family and {∅} boundary cases and the equivalence of cardinal bounds with natural-number counts. Exhaustive computations found no failures among all 3, 6, and 20 downward-closed families on ground sets of sizes 1, 2, and 3. A separate Lean proof confirms that choosing one dominating star is equivalent to allowing its center to depend on the intersecting subfamily, by maximizing star size. The cited page still records the problem as OPEN, matching the category. Scratch files are in /workspace/review/; the reviewed file was not modified.
